citations.review_text:
Man, what a ride. This is by far the best Telltale style show I've ever watched. It honestly felt like watching Edgerunners, just without quite as much suffering.

The story is fairly simple, but it's incredibly enjoyable from start to finish. The characters are masterfully written, and it's hard not to like every single one of them. The biggest highlight, though, is the dialogue. Sometimes it's clever, sometimes it's cringy, but it's almost always funny. If you told me the dialogue and characters were written by pre-DC James Gunn, I'd believe you.

The voice cast also did an excellent job of making the characters feel alive and three dimensional, well, except for Sonar, voiced by Moist Critical. I think Charlie's performance was terrible, hopefully he'll be recast or removed entirely from season 2. The soundtrack absolutely slaps. Never in a million years did I expect to hear Bershy in a AAA production like this.

The management minigame is a nice break between story bits. Even though I'm usually not a fan of time management games, I genuinely enjoyed it here, despite it being fairly basic. There's also a hacking minigame that's very similar to the one from Human Revolution. It's nothing special, but it does a decen job of making certain story moments and the management minigame more engaging.

I really wish I had watched Dispatch last year instead of putting it aside because of my superhero fatigue. That was a huge mistake. Honestly I think Dispatch should be 2025 GOTY rather than Expedition 33 and I absolutely adore E33.

It's been a few months since I finished this game, and figured I'd just now write this review. I did decide to wait until after all the episodes came out, so that I could just play through this in minimal sessions(did 2 episodes per day). All spoiler free thankfully.
[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
The main gameplay here is dispatching villains-to-be-heroes to help with different issues in the city this game takes place in. It very much is a strategy game here, where you have to decide which scenario is best for heroes to go to in order to actually solve the issue. As the game progressed it got a lot more fun, as I got [spoiler]more people to dispatch out[/spoiler], and you can level up people through different categories to put simply. Then of course there is the choose-your-own-story element. I haven't done this kind of gameplay in a long time, so it was great being able to do this again. Plus it gives variety from the base dispatching gameplay.
[h2]Story & Characters[/h2]
While a lot of this game is the strategic dispatching, the game also has a really enjoyable story. Not anything too crazy, but I overall loved the characters in the story. Especially with this being former villains becoming heroes, seeing their progression to heroism was great. As well as Robert's character progression throughout the story trying to be a hero again. Plus there is a love story involved between two women, Robert's boss Blonde Blazer and one of the former villains working for him, Invisigal. So that was also interesting choosing between which one I wanted Robert to go for.
[h2]Performance & Polish[/h2]
The game ran really well on my PC. Pretty sure a lot of the game is pre-recorded videos, so not a lot of intense rendering is needed here. Not sure about a potato PC but I'm sure a fairly low-end one like a decent work laptop could run the game. I don't remember if they had different performance options, but to at least run the game a somewhat lower end PC could do it. I also very much enjoyed the…

citations.review_text:
Incredible experience - my main complaint is that I need more! 

Make sure you're aware that the majority of this experience is watching the story (with periodic dialogue decisions) interspersed with the dispatch gameplay. The animation is gorgeous, the voice acting is excellent, the story is great... all in all, very enjoyable. 

If I had a complaint about gameplay, it'd be the hacking. Those segments feel unnecessary and tedious. Otherwise, 10/10 and I can't wait to try a new playthrough with different choices.
Fun and funny. Hate the hacking minigames, but the story is great.

citations.review_text:
I feel like I entered this game with too much expectations because all the normies say it's the greatest thing since jesus and all that, it's not, it's actually a pretty simple, widely accessible product, but they do what they do well, they deliver on what they set out to do, which seems to be a gamefied comic release, a comic where the good guys always win and nobody dies and everyone lived happily ever after, despite hiding behind a shield of profanity, nudity, and mature themes

EXPECT a well animated, well written casual story where choices matter(but not really)
DO NOT EXPECT depth or real consequences

It's fun, but that's about it, it could've been so much more, but it chose not to, and that's ok

I don't know why this game has such a high rating. This is really a short animated series with an occasional mini-game in which you pick which heroes from your roster to send on missions, and there is a simple mechanic of matching the heroes stats with the requirements of the mission. It really isn't complicated.
There is some rather pointless button clicking in the few combat sequences of the game, but these are little more than a distraction from watching the animated fights. 
You also get to make dialogue choices which don't massively impact the narrative, which is set with a single ending. These only seem to affect which character you may have a romantic interest in (don't expect anything more than a kissing scene) and small changes to being more of a hero/villain personality. 
TLDR: The GOOD = great animation with excellent voice acting, script and story.
The BAD = not really much of a game (expect to sit watching the screen for most of your time), with NO quick saves! WTF? Set save points is something Noah and his kids used to have on the Ark - get with the times and remedy this crap! 
Would I buy a sequel 'game'? Maybe, but only if it was on sale.

Dispatch has a cool management gameplay and interesting story to follow with diverse and likable characters, which making it a great game, but it's just "too safe" and never commit fully to anything.

First of all, Dispatch looks amazing. The style, the animations, characters and the effects looks like it's coming from an interactive comic book and this is just works on so many level. Then the gameplay is pretty interesting with the management part, where you need to send specific heroes to different distress calls and upgrade them along the way, and this doesn't get boring. The story is okay, although it has some clichés and can predict some moments, but overall it's enjoyable. The characters are diverse enough and somehow almost every one of them are fan favorites in their own way, it's fun to see them interacting on they own or with the other cast. Soundtrack and surprisingly very good and the voice actors were top notch. Controls were like 5 buttons on keyboard and mouse and that's about it, it's really easy.

Dispatch is a really great game and this is in my favorites without a doubt, but I can't really ignore the fact that how safe this game is trying to be. The thing is that the management aspect or the story could have been more, but it never commit to any of those. Management aspect certainly could have had more room for things to do and the story could have had more screen for certain characters, more meaningful story arcs for a few of them or to focus on some of the characters, and even there could have been more decisions which shape the story. I don't want to spoil and detail this too much, but I believe if you have played this game you sorta know what I mean here.

Don't get me wrong, I really enjoyed Dispatch and I even played it back to back another route because how interested I was in this game, which is very rare for me to replay something so soon, but this game is not without some missing pieces. I can definitely recommend this game to play for b…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes management mechanics involving dispatching heroes to handle various incidents or emergencies.

citations.review_text:
I had never played a game like Dispatch before, so I really didn't know what to expect. After finishing it, I can honestly say I had an amazing time!

The dispatching mechanic is a lot more fun than I expected. It starts off pretty relaxed, but once several incidents come in at the same time, things can get surprisingly hectic... I actually caught myself thinking ahead and trying to figure out the best way to handle everything. It never felt unfair though, just challenging enough to keep me engaged.

The biggest surprise for me was the story. It didn't really feel like playing a game most of the time. It felt more like watching a really good animated movie where I got to influence what happened through my decisions. I got attached to the characters much more than I expected and I was always looking forward to the next conversation or story moment.

My only small complaint is that I wish there had been a choice between a male and female protagonist. I know the story was clearly written around the main character, so I understand why they didn't include that option, but I still would have appreciated the choice.

Other than that, I genuinely loved it. It's funny, emotional, charming and just something different from the usual games I play. If you enjoy story-driven games where your choices matter and don't mind a bit of pressure while trying to keep everyone happy, I'd definitely recommend giving Dispatch a try, it's an amazing game.

Never fear, Captain Backlog is here! ([i]Admittedly much later than planned[/i]). Sworn protector of unplayed games and master of ignoring overwhelmingly positive reviews until everyone else has already had their way with it! I heard people praise this game, I saw the hype, I saw the reviews and still I somehow left it sitting there like an emergency call I forgot to answer. Then, much later than any responsible hero would admit, I finally started it:

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3749191729

You play as Robert Robertson, aka Mecha Man, a superhero whose suit gets wrecked so badly that he ends up sitting behind a desk, managing emergencies and trying to turn a chaotic team of ex-villains into actual heroes. The game switches between two main parts. One side feels like an interactive animated series, where you follow Robert and make choices for him during conversations and story moments. The other side puts you behind the desk as an actual dispatcher, deciding which team members to send out to different emergencies based on their skills, moods and super powers. During the dispatch sections, youll also run into hacking mini games, which add a bit more variety while youre already busy trying to keep this barely functional superhero team going.

For me, the best part of Dispatch is easily the writing. [b]KAPOW![/b] It has actual punch! Dispatch is stylish, heartfelt and really funny! Your team feels messy, dramatic and weirdly enough also lovable. Some of my favorites were Sonar, who is basically a man-bat in the process of becoming a bat-man (and still not the strangest person in the room). Punch Up is a short, ridiculously strong guy with a very special fighting move [spoiler][i](punching people in their loins with excessive force)[/i][/spoiler], which still makes me laugh just thinking about it. Then there is Malevola, who brings demon portal magic and a personality that made me laugh way more than I expected. All the characters add so much …

I've always been on the fence on these "animated movies remixed into interactive games". 

Dispatch is one of those games, similar to the style of Telltale (The Walking Dead, The Wolf Among Us, ...) and Quantic Dream (Fahrenheit, Hard Rain, ...) companies' games, at least in principle. I've finished the aforementioned four games, but didn't really 'love' them. 

Dispatch felt different, I really enjoyed it - might even say I 'loved' it. [spoiler] Okay fine, I did love The Wolf Among Us and Life is Strange, which are reasons why I look into games of this genre occasionally.[/spoiler]

I binge-gamed through Dispatch twice, but it's like a mix of watching a good superhero/-villain themed TV-show and an another part of light gaming. The voice actors are top notch (including stars like Jesse Pinkman's actor from Breaking Bad), and the characters, their dialogue, and story overall are good and incredibly immersive. There are only couple story telling details or cliches that rubbed me the wrong way, but I'm willing to overlook them as the whole was cohesive and entertaining.

There are basicly three "games" to be played within Dispatch:
- Make dialogue options, which have some effect on the story (usually 2-3 choices to take from, typical reactions to quick-time events in fights etc)
- Control superhero assignments, manage their time and stats when sending them out to perform superhero duties as the title Dispatcher
- Play a hacker minigame to help out your heroes, with light puzzle elements

I can recommend Dispatch highly if you fill in at least some of the following checkboxes:
- It's the kind of game you'd put on when you're tired and really instead should be going to sleep and don't want to be sweating over some "proper" sweaty try-hard game - and then you suddenly notice it's 4 in the morning because you just had to check out "just one more episode"
- You like superheroes in movies or comics; for example, it reminded me of a lighter version of the TV-show The Boys (=…

claims.claim: Reviewers state that dialogue and narrative choices have a limited impact on the overall story progression and endings.

citations.review_text:
I feel like I entered this game with too much expectations because all the normies say it's the greatest thing since jesus and all that, it's not, it's actually a pretty simple, widely accessible product, but they do what they do well, they deliver on what they set out to do, which seems to be a gamefied comic release, a comic where the good guys always win and nobody dies and everyone lived happily ever after, despite hiding behind a shield of profanity, nudity, and mature themes

EXPECT a well animated, well written casual story where choices matter(but not really)
DO NOT EXPECT depth or real consequences

It's fun, but that's about it, it could've been so much more, but it chose not to, and that's ok

All in all, it is a good game.. if you like narrative driven, barely any gameplay games.
The caracters are charming, jokes are.. not very smart, but also not annoying. The villan was great. The gameplay that is there, the dispaching, is actually quite entertaining if annoying at times. Some dispach shifts are meant to be failed even though possible to be beaten flawelessly.
My biggest problem is the price. 28 eur without discount seems a little too much. I would suggest getting it on discount. When i finished my first playthrough, i clocked in at 10.5h, at least 2-3h of which was me leaving the game running while i was doing some other chores and at least 1h of redoing some chapters to get some better dispaching results. My second playthrough was probably about 3h.
Now one could say that it is a game that you can replay trying different choices to get different results, but that is where the problems are, the consequences of your choices are minimal, basicly boiling down to which one of the two members you will have for the entire game, who you will romace (one of two options or none at all) and whether one of your team members will be good or maybe bad at the end. As a comparison i did a second playthrough trying to be as bad as possible, not only to my team members, but also fail every mission/qte i could and the ending was nearly identical as with a "good" ending. Talking about QTE-s, they are pointless in this game, you can fail all of them and almost nothing changes. Combine with the fact that there are no unlockable extras, like concept art and things like that, the price becomes too high.

who knew a game about answering phone calls would be fun?

summary - you play as robert, a person with no superpowers, who helps dispatch superheroes. a dispatcher is someone who answers phone calls and hear problems are. you assign a superhero based on who you think is best for the task. your team? a group of villains called the z-team

the characters and interaction between the characters is where the game really shines. i didn't feel like this was a superhero game. it was more about working with your team and the relationships you have with them

to my understanding, this company were the same people who worked on telltale's walking dead. and the ideas are very reminiscent. you'll branch off ideas, and sometimes you have to make decisions that impact the story later. and those decisions sometimes are irreversible. so if you have analysis paralysis, this game also is for you

i recommend playing this game at least another time to see alternatives, but honestly? playing it once is fine. you can watch youtube clips online and see what would've happened if you chose path b. fundamentally, nothing changes, but you'll get some interesting different flavor texts

one thing i didn't like is the game indirectly pushes you to a certain thing. i personally had no interest in said thing but not a deal breaker

a thing i'd love to see is an opportunity to just work on the dispatch calls themselves. that could be a mini in itself. that would be fun to just take as many calls as you want

i'm usually not a fan of a big cast because it creates bloat. but the gameplay and interaction with these characters felt smart, and the interplay among them really worked out. if dispatch 2 (or whtaever game comes out), i'd gladly wishlist it

- You like superheroes in movies or comics; for example, it reminded me of a lighter version of the TV-show The Boys (=…

PROS
- Excellent storytelling from beginning to end.
- Strong character writing and development.
- Interesting premise that immediately grabs your attention.
- Engaging management gameplay.
- Challenging hacking minigames.
- Story progression keeps the gameplay from feeling repetitive.
- Thoughtful accessibility options, including the ability to disable NSFW content in the settings for players who prefer a more comfortable experience.

CONS
- If you're not invested in the narrative, the gameplay may not be enough to keep you engaged.
- Lack of a New Game+ feature makes replaying for different choices or achievements more tedious than it should be.

VERDICT
I went into Dispatch almost completely blind. All I knew was that it was a choice-driven narrative game people kept recommending, and I intentionally avoided learning anything else. I'm really glad I did. Watching the story unfold naturally made every twist, every character, and every emotional moment hit so much harder. The gameplay does exactly what it needs to do: it supports the narrative without distracting from it. If you're looking for a story-driven game with memorable characters and meaningful character development, Dispatch is absolutely worth your time.

4/5

Really fun game overall. 9/10! Great voice acting, great animation, great characters and story writing and amazing character development. I like the gameplay as well, the dispatching mechanic is very unique and new to me as well as the hacking sequences...very fun! Only downside is that the ending was a little bit anticlimactic but I understand and I was still able to enjoy the game--replaying it about 3 times just to see all the outcomes and for full achievements.
